doc.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016

title: Kenton's band compared with Basie and Woody as 'whiter' bands
summary: Jenkins calls Kenton 'Wagnerian jazz', a heavy swing, and a mostly white band compared with Basie.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah. The Kenton band was not like that was it?

No, it wasn’t. Not by design necessarily, but Woody and Stan and even Buddy Rich, they were pretty white bands. Not by design necessarily. Stan had a couple of African- American guys in the band, but it was a pretty white band.
Do you think that black players would not be attracted that much to what Stan Kenton did?
Possibly. Because we called it kind of Wagnerian jazz you know. And I loved it. And Stan was very nice. He was one of the nicest leaders I’ve ever worked for. He was great.

But it was kind of heavy. It swung in its own way but certainly it was a different kind of swing than Bas’. But I don’t think the guys, like on Basie’s band, they were very respectful of it on Stan’s band, but it was sort of — it wasn’t a band — it seemed like it was sort of a whiter band, sort of like Woody.
